newsitem.title: USA: High 60-cent zinc needed in Yukon restart - Cominco.
newsitem.headline: High 60-cent zinc needed in Yukon restart - Cominco.

text.p: Zinc prices would need to sustain levels in the high-60-cent-a-pound range, before Cominco Ltd. and its joint venture partners could consider reopening the Sa Dena Has mine in the Yukon, a Cominco Ltd executive told Reuters.

The joint venture partners are planning to spend C$3.25 million in each 1997 and 1998 to to revamp the mine infrastructure to prepare for the restart, which would occur in the second quarter at the earliest, said Tony Keen, Cominco Ltd.'s general manager of Yukon operations.

"We would need to see a sustained zinc price in the high 60s to see a restart," Keen said. The London Metal Exchange zinc cash closing price was 72.30 cents a pound Wednesday. So far this year, the LME zinc closing cash price has averaged approximately 59.34 cents a lb.
At full production, the mine would produce 75,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates and 15,000 tonnes of lead concentrates.
Cominco holds a 25 percent stake in the mine. Teck Corp holds a 25 percent stake and Korea Zinc Co owns the remaining 50 percent.
The mine was commissioned by Curragh in 1991, but was mothballed in December 1992, because of its high operating costs and Curragh's financial condition, Keen said.
Keen wouldn't comment on the expected operating costs of the mine until the tender calls were completed. The company announced the calls Wednesday.
The concentrates would be sold in the Asia, Keen said, with Korea Zinc, being a logical smelter of the concentrates.
